plugins.description: The plugins the project switches on: each a module's name, or its name and the folder its package is in, relative to the project's main checkout. Without the key a project loads no plugins

siblings.description: Folders beside the project. A variable name follows the sibling's origin/main. An object exports the named variable to the run's checkout of the sibling: its revision pins a full Git commit, and its link names a folder beside the lane's checkout, ../FOLDER, that Queuekeeper links to that checkout before each lane for a build that reads the sibling by a relative path.

link.description: One folder beside the lane's checkout, ../FOLDER: Queuekeeper makes it a link to the run's checkout of the sibling, replacing nothing but a missing path, a link whose target is gone or a link it made, and never a folder or a link a person made

gitHooks.description: The folder of the project's tracked Git hooks, relative to the checkout's top, such as .githooks. qk doctor sets core.hooksPath to it where it is unset, as in a fresh clone, and warns where it names another folder

simulatorPool.description: The name every member of the project's simulator pool starts with, as in 'NAME iPhone 17 Pro 1'; required with the simulator-pool capability

emulatorPool.description: The Android plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_android: the name every member of the project's emulator pool starts with, as in 'NAME_Pixel_8_API_36_1'

emulatorRetention.description: The Android plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_android: the emulator pool's retention policy, which qk emulator-pool reap applies on a Mac whose AVD inventory reads as verified. Off when left out

deleteUnused.description: Delete a pool member whose recorded last use is more than unusedDays old, and a template whose kind has no member left, never the pool's last template, recording each deletion; false when left out

unusedDays.description: How many days a member stays unused before the policy deletes it; 14 when left out

android.description: The Android plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_android: the Gradle build whose app and instrumented tests qk emulator-tests builds and runs

directory.description: The Gradle project's folder, the one with gradlew, relative to the checkout; the checkout itself when left out

module.description: The application module, as a Gradle project path without its leading colon, such as 'app' or 'feature:reader'; app when left out

variant.description: The build variant, such as 'debug' or 'freeDebug'; debug when left out

gradleArguments.description: Words added to every Gradle command, never shell source

unity.description: The Unity plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_unity: where its Unity project is, and the window layout a new worktree's editor starts with

project.description: The folder that holds ProjectSettings, relative to the checkout, such as 'lab'; the checkout itself when left out

layout.description: A window layout (.dwlt), relative to the checkout, that qk unity open gives a worktree with none of its own before its first launch

pullRequests.description: How a project that integrates through pull requests admits or checks them

label.description: The label a person adds to a pull request to queue it (default queue)

lanes.description: The lanes qk pr check runs on a pull request by itself, in a pull-request project (default gate)

oneOf.description: A lane: a command and how it runs
A lane group: other lanes run side by side under its one admission

inputs.description: For a gate lane, one of queue.lanes or else gate, or a lane of a gate lane group: globs of the repository-relative paths that affect it (* and ? within one directory, ** across any number). A batch runs the lane only when one of its changed paths matches one, and a batch that selects no gate lane skips the gate, running its preflight and docs lanes as a batch of unread paths does. A gate lane without inputs runs for every change. A group's lanes that give inputs are chosen among by a batch's paths, under the group's one admission; a group gives its own or its lanes do, never both. queuekeeper.json and queuekeeper-workspace.json affect every lane. Read from main

parallel.description: A lane group's lanes, each a lane with a command, which run side by side under the group's one admission; the group needs the heaviest resource among them

jobs.description: How many of a lane group's lanes run at once, from 1 to their number; without it, all of them

failFast.description: Whether a lane group ends at its first failed lane: the lanes still running are stopped as their timeout would stop them, the rest never start, and each is reported cut short, with no verdict of its own. The group fails. A merge queue gate cut short this way never lands as flaky: a batch whose failed tests then pass alone gates again, once for its commit, and bisects if it stops so again. Left out or false, every lane runs to its own end

command.description: The lane's command, its words run with no shell. A first word that is the bare word qk, as in ["qk", "unittest", "-s", "tests"], runs Queuekeeper's own command: qk run starts it as the selected Queuekeeper checkout's bin/qk with --project, that checkout being the one QUEUEKEEPER_ROOT names, else the one running, on the Mac that runs the lane

environmentInputs.description: Caller environment variable names the lane's command reads. After a remote attempt at the lane's command, Queuekeeper warns when the calling shell set a listed name that the dispatch omitted. The setting adds a warning only. Set it on the member lane of a group

resource.description: The admission the lane takes, first come, first served, another Mac first (the owner's decision, 2026-11-07): heavy, one slot, which light, the older name of a short check, and no resource mean too; exclusive, the host to itself; or self, for a lane whose script admits each of its parts itself, which qk run runs where it starts, unadmitted

minimumTests.description: A floor typed by hand: the fewest executed tests the lane's log must report for a whole run that exits 0 to pass; a skipped test counts toward none. Without it, a log that reports a count must report one test that ran, and a whole run must execute as many as the lane's last passing whole run on main on the same Mac, unless a commit since says Tests-Removed: LANE. With exactTests, the count the run must equal

exactTests.description: Whether a whole run of the lane must execute exactly its minimumTests, which the lane must then give: any other count fails, naming the count observed, so that adding, deleting or renaming a test the lane selects fails the lane instead of leaving minimumTests wrong. Left out or false, minimumTests is a floor. A lane that says true is held to this count instead of its history. A run with arguments needs one test, or its --expect, as before

arguments.description: Whether the lane's command takes arguments. A lane that says false selects its own tests: qk run LANE -- ARGUMENTS, and --repeat, whose series reaches the command as arguments, are refused at once with exit status 2, before the lane is staged, admitted or sent to another Mac. Left out or true, the arguments are appended to the command

testAllowance.description: The seconds the lane's own script allows one test, such as the XCTest allowance a script that runs xcodebuild test passes itself. A direct run on another Mac shows it in its clock line, which cannot read it from the script. A runner whose plugin reads its allowance from its arguments, such as qk simulator-tests, shows that instead. It sets no limit

sandbox.description: Run an admitted lane's command, and its compileFirst, under a macOS Seatbelt sandbox (sandbox-exec) made on the Mac that runs it: it writes only to the checkout it runs in, its git directory, its run's directory, the temporary and cache folders and the paths write names, and reaches the network only as network says, by default not at all. true takes the defaults. A self lane cannot have one, and the Apple plugin refuses one for a lane that runs Xcode or SwiftPM, which apply sandboxes of their own and cannot inside another

write.description: Further folders the command may write to: absolute, ~/..., or relative to the checkout

network.description: What the command may reach; none when empty or absent. localhost, localhost:PORT, HOST:PORT or *.DOMAIN:PORT for a host reached through the lane's filtering proxy, *:PORT for any host on a port, * for any, or a unix socket's absolute path

failedTests.description: Where a lane that is not qk unittest names its failed tests, so that the merge queue reruns each alone before a bisect. A lane whose plugin names them, as a qk unity test lane's, gives paths alone; any other needs results and rerun.

results.description: The JUnit XML file the lane writes, as a path relative to its results folder, QUEUEKEEPER_RESULTS_DIR.

rerun.description: The argv that reruns one test alone, with {test} for its name, classname.name from the JUnit XML.

paths.description: The files the lane's tests depend on, each a file or a directory ending in /. A batch whose failed tests all pass alone lands only when it changes none of them; with none listed, it bisects.

timing.description: The lane's timing guidance against its baseline, the p90 of its recent passing runs on the Mac that runs it: a live warning past it, and an optional fail threshold relative to it.

warn.description: Warn while the lane runs past its baseline; true unless false.

fail.description: Fail the lane once it runs this far past its baseline, such as +25% or +2m.

minSamples.description: The passing runs the baseline needs before the fail threshold applies; 10 unless given.

targetMinutes.description: How long the lane is meant to take, in minutes, inside its timeout. A run that ends, passing or failing, past it warns, naming the lane, its time and its target; nothing fails or stops for it. Any lane with a command takes it, a lane group's members too, and config refuses one past the lane's timeout

notice.description: What an agent is shown when the lane's timeout, stall bound or timing fail threshold stops it. The default says not to raise the limit just to make the gate pass.

stall.description: Opt-in quiet monitoring for an admitted leaf lane. Report-only by default; stopping requires a healthy-run measurement and a reviewed bound.

primaryControl.description: Explicitly declare that the supervised primary process only coordinates descendant work. Its CPU cannot mask quiet descendants; no descendants leaves the observation unavailable. Omit for serial or primary-process computation.

notice.description: What an agent is shown when the stall bound stops the lane, in place of the lane's notice.

foreground.description: The lane takes a Mac's screen, keyboard, pointer, focus or speech, as Mac VoiceOver and Mac XCUITest lanes do. It needs a heavy or exclusive resource. qk run sends it to another Mac, which queuekeeper takes the foreground of for the run, waiting while another run holds it, and never to this Mac; qk run --here, or here, runs it on this Mac only for the session holding mac-foreground within the owner's window

apps.description: A foreground lane's app under test, each name as a crash-report alert names the process that quit, such as EPUBLib. A failed run during which queuekeeper cleared a crash-report alert for another process, one that stood longer than one look, is unmeasured; one for these, or for a process queuekeeper cannot name, stays failed

here.description: Why an admitted lane runs only on this Mac rather than on another Mac of the farm: a physical device, or a measurement tied to this Mac's hardware, such as goldens rendered on its GPU. Simulator, background Mac UI and foreground lanes go to another Mac like the rest. A lane group that runs such a lane stays here with it

model.description: A heavy lane that runs a model: on-device generation, another local generative model on the GPU, or Core ML whose compute units include the GPU. qk run admits it with one slot and the host's model lock, so model runs exclude each other while other heavy work runs beside them. A lane group that runs it needs model too, or an exclusive resource, and a group that runs two or more needs jobs 1. A model run that is timed or compared with a baseline is exclusive instead, which holds the model already

display.description: The Mac desktop plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_mac_desktop or a plugin that requires it, such as queuekeeper_apple. A heavy or exclusive lane whose tests wait for what the display's refresh times, such as a scroll view's animation: qk run runs its command, on any Mac and in a lane group too, under a one-second caffeinate -u, which wakes a sleeping display behind a lock too, and then caffeinate -d, which keeps it on for the command's life, and the lane's receipt shows them in its command. Neither unlocks the screen, so a test that reads its tree through the accessibility API still needs an unlocked one

unity.description: The Unity plugin's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_unity. A lane whose command runs the project's Unity editor: qk run runs its command under qk unity ready --, which checks on the Mac that runs it that an editor is installed, that no editor has the project open, that no stale lock is left and that no orphaned licensing helper remains, and ends the lane unmeasured, with nothing run, when one of them does not hold. An exclusive lane also ends unmeasured while an editor on that Mac is in Play mode

labels.description: What an admitted lane needs of the Mac that runs it, such as a license or a piece of hardware: it runs only on a Mac whose own settings, mac-settings.json beside its admission limits, list every one of these labels. A Mac's settings name no lane and a lane names no Mac. A lane group needs the labels of its lanes as well as its own

budgetMinutes.description: The gate lane's time budget in minutes, from its measured time. When the median wall time of its recent passing runs in the merge queue exceeds it, qk land and qk doctor warn and name its slowest parts. Only the gate lane takes it

deviceRunMinutes.description: Minimum admission estimate in minutes for the full device lane, including the build, every device, and cleanup inside the lane. The reservation's own cleanup allowance is added separately

wholeHost.description: A heavy lane that is a Mac's work, such as a gate that runs the project's suites side by side: it takes every guaranteed slot of the Mac it runs on, so a second such lane never runs beside it there, and qk run sends it to the Mac that has them all free, while a lighter heavy lane still shares. A lane group that runs it needs wholeHost too, or an exclusive resource, which holds the host already

idioms.description: Why the lane runs its whole selection on an iPhone and an iPad simulator: that every class it selects depends on the idiom, and where the project classifies them. Without it, qk doctor warns of a lane whose command names both with --device, outside release.lanes

dimensions.description: Why the lane runs its whole selection once per appearance or content size, such as that it selects only a view's snapshot tests. Without it, qk doctor warns of a lane whose command names two appearances or content sizes, or another lane's command but for them, outside release.lanes

devices.description: The device-record entries, such as iPhone, that a lane's script uses when its command is not qk device-pass, whose --device options say so: the lane waits for admission only until the last start that can finish within the window the session holds them for. It needs an admitted lane

unlockedScreen.description: A lane whose tests need an unlocked console screen, such as one that reads its own tree through the accessibility API; a lane group that runs such a lane says so too. queuekeeper places it only on a Mac whose screen reads unlocked, locked and unknown alike counting as no room for it, and otherwise it waits instead of running unmeasured. It needs an admitted lane

disk.description: The lane's own free disk space settings, which take the place of the project's disk for it, and a lane group's for the lanes it runs under its one admission

startFreeGB.description: The GiB free on the data volume and the checkout's volume that the lane waits for before admission when it fills the disk: a whole-host or exclusive lane, or one with compileFirst. It takes the place of the project's disk.startFreeGB; QUEUEKEEPER_START_FREE_GB, when set, overrides both. 0 waits for none

compileFirst.description: An argv that compiles the lane's test target, such as xcodebuild build-for-testing on the derived data its command uses. It runs before the command in the lane's one admission and timeout, and a failure ends the run as build-failed with no test run. It needs an admitted lane, and a group runs its lanes' commands without it

disk.description: The project's free disk space settings

startFreeGB.description: The GiB free on the data volume and the checkout's volume that each of the project's lanes that fills the disk (a whole-host or exclusive lane, or one with compileFirst) waits for before admission, unless the lane gives its own disk.startFreeGB; QUEUEKEEPER_START_FREE_GB, when set, overrides both. Without either, 10. Set it higher for a project whose builds and result bundles take tens of GiB. 0 waits for none

testLanes.description: What qk doctor's check that every test has a lane cannot work out for itself

skip.description: Test paths kept as records, not counted as coverage, each mapped to the reason; a key ending in / is a directory

selects.description: For a lane whose command the check cannot read, the paths its tests are under; a key ending in / is a directory, and an empty list says the lane runs no test

citations.description: true has qk docs check also check citations of a document by path and section title, as in (doc/setup.md, Install), or by path and anchor, in the project's Markdown and source files: each must name a document of this checkout and a heading or bold lead-in of it. Off unless set

lanes.description: The lanes a batch passes before it lands, in order. Without it, the lane named gate

addOnlyJson.description: Literal repository-relative JSON files whose conflicts the queue may settle when both sides only add keys to the selected object. Each value lists the object keys from the root to that object. An empty array selects the file's root object. Only main's setting applies

reuseGate.description: Gate lanes whose whole local pass may be reused, mapped to read-only commands that identify their execution inputs. Only main's setting applies

hookCoveredBy.description: The queue lanes that cover the pre-push hook, each with what of the hook it runs. With it, the queue pushes without running the hook

unread.description: The paths no code lane reads. A batch that changes only these runs the docs lanes in place of the gate, and main changing one a passed batch does not touch leaves its result standing. The conventional Markdown defaults, the root README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md and Markdown under doc/ and docs/, count unless defaults is false, as do the root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md while the docs lane is the toolkit's qk docs check. False gates every batch and carries nothing over. Replaced docsOnly and carryOver, which are refused

paths.description: Each path, a directory ending in /, with why no code lane reads it; these add to the Markdown defaults, and are how a project names any other documentation folder, such as guides/. A path that a few small checks do read gives an object of why and lanes, those checks' lanes, which a docs-only batch changing it runs too; such a path never carries over a passed result

lanes.description: The lanes that read this path, which a docs-only batch changing it runs as well as queue.unread.lanes; never gate

exclude.description: Paths among paths or the Markdown defaults that code or tests do read, with why; these always gate

lanes.description: The lanes a batch of unread paths runs instead, in order; never gate

defaults.description: False drops the conventional Markdown defaults and the root agent instructions, so that only paths counts

fullRun.description: When the queue's worker, once the queue has drained, gates main whole, every gate lane and every lane of a group, for the landings whose gates their paths narrowed by lane inputs and that no whole gate has covered since. A failure holds the queue and names the first such landing at which the failed lane fails. False never runs it. Read from main

landings.description: How many such landings may wait for the full run; 5 where unset

minutes.description: How many minutes the oldest such landing may wait for it; 240 where unset

noVerdictRuns.description: How many runs in a row of a batch's gate may give no verdict (exit 3, 75 or 78) before the batch comes back; 3 where it is unset. Read from main, never from a branch

followLandings.description: true has the queue fast-forward the project's main checkout to origin/main after each landing, when it is on main, clean and nothing runs from it: for a checkout other projects read, such as the folder a plugin loads from. Read from main

preflight.description: The project's preflight lanes, in order: cheap checks, each one command, that qk land runs on an entry replayed onto origin/main before it queues it, refusing it on a finding (exit 1), and that the queue runs first in every round, ungated landing and docs-only batch. [] or leaving it out for none. Read from main

quick.description: Quick checks: lanes the merge queue's worker runs in its checkout without admission, as it runs the preflight lanes and qk docs check, wherever a round runs them. Each must be "resource": "light", one command (no lane group, foreground, whole-host, model or unlocked-screen lane) and give a timeout of 60 or less, and none may be gate, provision or one of queue.lanes. One that runs past 60 s runs again admitted. A project's own docs lane meeting the same test is a quick check without being listed. [] or leaving it out for none. Read from main

carryOverChecks.description: Commands that must pass on the rebased tree before a passed result carries over a move of main; any other outcome gates again, with no blame

command.description: An argv list, never shell source. {base} in a word is the commit the result passed on

paths.description: Run only when main moved one of these paths, a directory ending in /. Without it, on every carry-over

app.description: The app qk app keeps and runs: the last good build of each platform, kept on this Mac

project.description: The Xcode project, a path inside the checkout

workspace.description: The Xcode workspace, a path inside the checkout

directory.description: Where the project is and the build runs, inside the checkout. Without it, the checkout's top

configuration.description: The build configuration. Without it, Debug

prepare.description: What runs in directory before each build, such as generating the project: one command as an argument list, or a list of them run in order

oneOf.description: One command, as an argument list
Several commands, each an argument list, run in order

scheme.description: The scheme that builds the app

product.description: The built app's file name, such as Name.app; needed only when the build makes more than one app

settings.description: Build settings given on xcodebuild's command line, such as DEVELOPMENT_TEAM

afterLanding.description: Whether the merge queue keeps a build of it after each gated landing. Without it, true

scheme.description: The scheme that builds the app

product.description: The built app's file name, such as Name.app; needed only when the build makes more than one app

settings.description: Build settings given on xcodebuild's command line, such as DEVELOPMENT_TEAM

afterLanding.description: Whether the merge queue keeps a build of it after each gated landing. Without it, false

links.description: Checkouts beside the project that its build names by a relative path, such as ../NAME, each linked beside the kept source

lanes.description: The release checks, each a lane of its own, which run after gate on the release commit; qk release requires a pass of each at the commit, or the owner's waiver of its failure. Never gate, which qk release checks first, nor any lane a landing runs: the preflight lanes, provision, queue.lanes or gate, queue.unread.lanes, or a member of a group among them

maxCommits.description: The code commits main may hold since a release lane's last pass before the checkpoint calls that lane due. Without it, the toolkit's default

maxDays.description: The days since a release lane's last pass before the checkpoint calls that lane due. Without it, the toolkit's default

limits.description: A release lane's own maxCommits or maxDays, in place of release.maxCommits or release.maxDays, keyed by a lane in release.lanes

maxCommits.description: The code commits since this lane's last pass before it is due

maxDays.description: The days since this lane's last pass before it is due
